key_insight: The paper shows that discrete Morse and cobordism ideas can be used to extract stable structural guidance for graph diffusion models, improving how they generate and forecast graph data.
engineering_relevance: For graph ML systems, MG-Diff offers a topology-aware way to guide diffusion models that may improve robustness and performance on spatio-temporal forecasting and graph regeneration tasks.
method: Introduce cobordism-inspired structure to interpret graph-generating processes.
Use discrete Morse theory to derive induced diffusion guidance for graph diffusion models.
Provide stability guarantees under small perturbations when a positive decision gap holds.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports applications to spatio-temporal graph forecasting and graph regeneration, where the proposed pipeline MG-Diff is used to demonstrate utility.
watch_item: The stability and guarantees depend on a positive decision gap, so performance may degrade when that separation is weak or noisy.
paper_title: Graph Representation via Elements of Discrete Morse and Cobordism Theories
